$comment: Single authority for OS-level file associations (AGENTS.md iron rule 9).
Everything below is derived from this file: the Linux Flatpak .desktop MimeType
line, the AppStream <mediatype> list, the shared-mime-info XML the Flatpak ships,
the Android bundle.fileAssociations, the macOS Info.plist CFBundleDocumentTypes,
and scripts/test-file-associations.py, which fails when any carrier drifts.
The in-app open pickers keep their own per-platform OPEN_EXTENSIONS arrays (they
also admit .rfa/.rft so the RVT adapter can refuse family files by name); this
file must list the same extension set, and the gate compares them.
MIME choices (2026-11-13):
* dwg/dxf/obj/stl are standard in shared-mime-info; do not redefine them.
* model/step only exists in shared-mime-info >= 2.5, so it is shipped here too.
* model/ply and model/off have no standard type; application/x-ply is Cura's
legacy name and is kept as an alias.
* .coff is a Geomview OFF variant. Never reuse application/x-coff: since
shared-mime-info 2.5 that is Windows object code with globs *.o and *.obj.
* application/x-ifc matches Bonsai/IfcOpenShell. It carries NO magic here:
IFC and STEP both start with `ISO-10303-21;`, and the IFC magic would mistype
.step files. The glob is the discriminator.
* Revit documents are private types with globs only: all four are OLE/CFB
containers, so magic cannot tell a project from a family.
* .skp uses the de-facto application/vnd.sketchup.skp with a glob only (the
UTF-16LE signature is not expressible as a compact magic pattern).
* .dgn has no compact magic here: V8 is an OLE/CFB container (same story as
Revit) and the V7 element header is too short to discriminate. The glob is
the discriminator; the importer sniffs bytes instead of trusting the
extension.
* application/octet-stream is added on Android only: content providers routinely
report CAD files as octet-stream, and without it 'Open with' never matches.
Windows is deliberately absent: the release is a zip of executables with no
installer, and registry associations can only be written by an installer. See
docs/windows-app.md.
